title: The player who was in two games
blurb: Ticket claims were not atomic and failures stranded tickets.
prompt: A player spawned into two matches simultaneously, because the draft claimed tickets one at a time and a retry rebuilt a roster from the same pool, and a failed server allocation left a whole roster's tickets claimed forever. Review it, fix it, and prove claims are all-or-nothing and releases are certain.
aiNote: The draft claims tickets sequentially, so a mid-claim failure or a concurrent matchmaker leaves one player in two rosters, and a failed allocation never releases the claimed tickets, stranding players in a queue position that no longer exists.
testIdea: Race two matchmakers over an overlapping pool and assert no player appears twice; fail allocation and assert every participant ticket returns to the pool and can be matched again; count pool depth against the ticket set.
followUps: What skill delta keeps matches fast and fair?
How long may a player wait before the pool widens?
What does an abandoned match owe its participants?
